title: ConversationSettings
description: Talking with an inhabitant (B6 R13, A1342): limits of the exchange and how understanding and the relation to the player change by outcome. The core computes every change from these rules; the AI only proposes the answer (B2462). Values are placeholders until Marcel's word.

deadline_ms.description: Deadline of a conversation request for the AI service.

no_answer_after_hours.description: Game hours after which an unanswered sentence counts as no answer (calm hint, R16).

recent_lines_max.description: How many recent lines an inhabitant keeps and sends as context.

history_lines_max.description: How many lines of its conversations with the player an inhabitant keeps for its memory page (B8 R16, B2518: old conversations, nothing invented), oldest dropped first; kept in the save game. Omitted or 0 = no history beyond the recent lines.

understanding_start.description: Understanding of the player at the start (gestures before words, D333).

fear_start.description: Fear of the player at the start.

refund_on_no_answer.description: Give the favour back when no answer comes (service off, timeout).

log_max_entries.description: Most conversation log entries kept (newest first stay; those of sentences still waiting are always kept). Older ones leave the save, so a replay reaches back only this far (review GW1 #128).

praise.description: A1538 (B6 R21, B2678): what praise of the player does when the service classified the player's text as praise (conversation-response voice.kind 'praise') and the inhabitant understood it (reply or gesture) - on top of the outcome's own changes, at most once per every_minutes. Omitted = praise does nothing.

naming.description: A1538/A1617 (B2678): what a naming does when the service passes one (the player pointed at a thing the inhabitant sees and wrote its word) and the inhabitant understood (reply or gesture): the word goes into its memory (event word_heard) - a name proposal by trust comes with A1536 - and its understanding grows by understanding. Omitted = a naming does nothing.

tip.description: A1536 (B6 R20, B2830, D1203 section 4): how sure an inhabitant is of what the player's voice says a thing is like - base + trust x its trust in the player + awe x its awe + fear x its fear, at most max (a guess, never sure). A belief it holds more surely stays. Placeholders (TL). Absent = a tip changes no belief.

proven_trust.description: Spec 31 acceptance 15: trust change toward the player when the inhabitant's own doing proves a tip true (placeholder). Omitted = 0.

failed_trust.description: The same when its doing shows the tip false (placeholder, negative). Omitted = 0.

dialogue.description: A1735 (B2782, D1119): a talk between two inhabitants. When one starts one of the actions with another inhabitant as target (awake and in reach - the core checked), the core sends a job of kind dialogue; the turns that pass its checks become said events of both, with target, turn and turns. A talk has no effect on the world: needs and relationship work through the action as before. Omitted = no dialogue jobs (talking stays without words).

understanding.description: Change of understanding when an exchange ends this way (computed by the core, never taken from the answer, B2462).

affection.description: Change of affection towards the player.

trust.description: Change of trust towards the player.

respect.description: Change of respect (awe) towards the player.

fear.description: Change of fear of the player.

every_minutes.description: Praise counts at most once in this many game minutes per inhabitant (calm world, B2466).

actions.description: Action ids (vocabulary actions, target inhabitant) whose start sends a dialogue job.

max_words.description: Words per turn at most (B2782: 14); a longer turn ends the talk there.

per_pair_hours.description: At most one dialogue job per pair within this many game hours (D1119 #6); the other talks stay without words. 0 = no limit.

job_priority.description: Priority of the job (higher runs first; low, the game waits for nothing).

answer_within_hours.description: Game hours a dialogue job may take; a later answer is dropped (the two went on without words), so no open job stays for ever.
